ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the line AC passing through the point $C(0, 12)$ intersects with the line OA at the point $A(8, 4)$. What is the area of $\triangle OAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $AH \perp OC$ at H, as shown in the diagram:\\
$\because A\left(8, 4\right)$ and $AH \perp OC$,\\
$\therefore AH=8$,\\
$\because C\left(0, 12\right)$,\\
$\therefore OC=12$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle OAC}=\frac{1}{2}OC \cdot AH=\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 8=\boxed{48}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure is a plane rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, C is located above the y-axis, A is the intersection point of the oblique line passing through O and the oblique line passing through C, and one side OC of triangle OAC is on the y-axis. Then reason: according to the specified method, choose OC as the base of triangle OAC. Given in the problem C(0,12), OC is the vertical line segment from O(0,0) to C(0,12), so OC=12. Given in the problem A(8,4), the perpendicular distance from point A to the vertical line OC (that is, the y-axis) is equal to the absolute value of its x-coordinate, which is 8. Therefore the area of the triangle S=1/2×OC×height=1/2×12×8=48.
